marana/hydro-jetting.intro:
Hydro jetting uses high-pressure water to scour the inside of a drain or sewer line. A cable punches a hole through a clog. Jetting cleans the pipe wall along its full length. That makes it a strong option for repeat clogs caused by grease, scale, or roots.

In Marana, hard water scale and kitchen grease are common reasons homeowners need it. Continental Ranch homes with mature trees near the sewer line may also have roots in the lateral. We camera inspect first, because jetting pressure can make a cracked or separated pipe worse. Homes on septic toward Avra Valley need a different approach, which we explain on the visit. You see the pipe on camera before and after, so you know exactly what was cleaned.

localFactors.title: Scale on Pipe Walls
localFactors.body: Hard water leaves a mineral layer inside drain pipes. A cable passes through it, but jetting can strip it back toward the pipe's full diameter. That slows down the next clog.

localFactors.title: Grease in Long Kitchen Lines
localFactors.body: Grease cools and hardens on the pipe wall, especially in long runs from the kitchen to the cleanout. Jetting removes it along the whole run. Scraping plates into the trash slows the buildup.

localFactors.title: Camera Check Comes First
localFactors.body: Jetting can make a cracked or separated pipe worse. We camera inspect Marana lines before jetting, especially older laterals near mature trees. If the pipe is damaged, we recommend repair instead.

localFactors.title: Septic Systems Need Care
localFactors.body: On septic properties toward Avra Valley and Picture Rocks, the line from the house to the tank can be jetted. The tank and drain field are a separate system. Jetting is for the line, not the drain field.

whatWeDo: We camera inspect the line to confirm the cause and make sure the pipe can handle the pressure.
We quote the jetting job upfront and explain what it will and will not fix.
We feed the jetting hose from a cleanout and work it through the line, scouring grease, scale, and roots.
We run a second camera pass so you can see the cleaned pipe.
We point out any spots that may need repair down the road.

faqs.question: When is hydro jetting better than regular drain cleaning?
faqs.answer: Jetting makes sense when clogs keep coming back or when grease, scale, or roots line the pipe. Regular cabling is fine for a single clog like a hair blockage. If the same line has needed clearing more than once this year, ask about jetting.

faqs.question: Is hydro jetting safe for my pipes?
faqs.answer: For pipe in sound condition, yes. It can make a cracked or separated pipe worse, which is why we inspect with a camera first. If we see damage, we tell you and suggest a repair instead.

faqs.question: Does hydro jetting get rid of roots in my sewer line for good?
faqs.answer: It removes them, but roots usually grow back through the same joint or crack. Jetting buys time. A lasting fix means repairing the spot where the roots get in.

It is not a whole-house treatment. A water softener handles hardness throughout the home, while RO focuses on the water you drink.

Marana homes get water from different providers depending on location, and some rural properties use private wells. That affects what your water contains and how you set up the system. Hard water also wears RO membranes faster, so homes with a softener ahead of the RO tend to get longer membrane life. We look at your sink space, water source and drain, then give you an upfront price.

localFactors.title: Hard water and membrane life
localFactors.body: Minerals in Marana's water can scale an RO membrane over time. A softener upstream reduces that buildup, and we set filter change intervals based on your setup.

localFactors.title: Different water sources
localFactors.body: Marana is served by more than one water provider, and homes toward Avra Valley may be on wells. Check your provider's water quality report, and test well water before choosing filters.

localFactors.title: Ice makers and garage fridges

localFactors.title: Drain space under the sink

faqs.question: Do I need reverse osmosis if I already have a softener in Marana?

faqs.question: Can you connect RO to the ice maker in my Saguaro Bloom kitchen?

faqs.question: Is reverse osmosis a good fit for a well near Avra Valley?

Newer Gladden Farms and Saguaro Bloom homes sometimes have construction debris or settled sections. An inspection is a diagnosis, not a repair. localFactors.title: Roots at joints
localFactors.body: Mesquite and palo verde trees planted in 1990s Continental Ranch yards are now mature. Their roots seek out small gaps at pipe joints, and the camera shows exactly where they enter.

localFactors.title: Settlement and sags

localFactors.title: Buying a resale home
localFactors.body: Many Marana homes change hands each year. A camera inspection before closing can reveal sewer issues that a general home inspection does not cover.

localFactors.title: Lines running to septic
localFactors.body: On properties near Picture Rocks and Avra Valley, the camera can follow the line from the house to the septic tank inlet. It helps separate a line problem from a tank or drain field problem.

faqs.question: Should I get a sewer camera inspection before buying a home in Marana?
faqs.answer: It is a good idea, especially for homes from the 1990s or with mature trees near the sewer line. Standard home inspections usually do not look inside the main line. The video gives you facts to use before closing.

faqs.question: Why does my newer Gladden Farms home keep backing up?
faqs.answer: Newer lines can still have problems, such as construction debris, a settled section or a poorly sloped joint. A camera inspection shows the cause so you are not paying for repeated drain cleaning.

faqs.question: Do I get a copy of the sewer camera footage?

marana/sewer-line-repair.metaTitle: Sewer Line Repair in Marana, AZ | Wood's Plumbing

Your sewer lateral carries everything from the house to the sewer main. When it cracks, sags, or fills with roots, drains keep backing up no matter how often you clear them. The first step is a camera inspection so we can see what is going on inside the pipe.

Marana laterals differ by area. Continental Ranch lines date to the 1990s and 2000s. Even plastic pipe of that age can sag or separate when soil settles or roots get in. Newer Gladden Farms and Saguaro Bloom lines are less likely to fail but can be damaged during landscaping work. Rural homes toward Picture Rocks and Avra Valley often run to a septic tank, which changes the repair. We show you the camera footage and quote repairs upfront.

localFactors.title: Roots From Desert Trees
localFactors.body: Mesquite, palo verde, and other trees planted near the front yard seek out water at sewer joints. Roots enter through small gaps and grow into a mat that catches waste. Repeated slow drains in spring and summer can be a sign.

localFactors.title: Soil Settling and Sags
localFactors.body: Expansive soils and caliche in the region can shift after heavy monsoon rains. A low spot, or belly, in the lateral holds water and waste. Backups that keep returning to the same place often point to a sag.

localFactors.title: Septic Lines Near Picture Rocks
localFactors.body: Homes on septic toward Picture Rocks and Avra Valley have a line from the house to a tank instead of a sewer lateral. A backup there can be the line or the tank. We check the line and tell you when to call a septic pumping company.

localFactors.title: Who Owns Which Section
localFactors.body: The homeowner is generally responsible for the lateral from the house to the connection at the main. Details can differ between town and county sewer areas. We help you figure out where your responsibility ends.

whatWeDo: We run a camera through the line from a cleanout and record the footage.
We locate any break, sag, or root intrusion and mark its depth and position in the yard.
We explain the options, such as a section repair or a full lateral replacement, and quote each upfront.
We excavate and repair or replace the damaged pipe, with proper bedding so it does not sag again.
We run a final camera pass and a water test to confirm the line flows freely.

faqs.question: How do I know if it is a sewer line problem and not just a clog?
faqs.answer: If several drains back up at once, especially a tub or shower when you flush, the problem is likely in the main line. Gurgling toilets and sewer odor in the yard are other signs. A camera inspection confirms it.

faqs.question: Will repairing the sewer line tear up my Marana yard?
faqs.answer: Traditional repair means digging down to the damaged section, so part of the yard gets disturbed. Desert rock landscaping can usually be raked back into place more easily than lawn or pavers. We show you where we need to dig before starting.

faqs.question: Do I call the town or a plumber when my sewer backs up?
faqs.answer: Ask your neighbors first. If several homes are backing up, call your sewer provider, since the main may be blocked. If just your home is affected, the problem is likely in your lateral, so call a plumber.

marana/slab-leak-detection.metaTitle: Slab Leak Detection in Marana, AZ | Wood's Plumbing
marana/slab-leak-detection.metaDescription: Slab leak detection in Marana. Warm tile, a meter that keeps moving, or wet baseboards? We pinpoint leaks under the concrete. Call (520) 682-2233.
marana/slab-leak-detection.intro:
Most Marana homes sit on concrete slabs, with water lines running under or through the concrete. When one of those lines leaks, the early signs are subtle. A warm spot on tile, the hiss of running water, or a meter that never stops moving are common. Wet carpet along a baseboard is another.

Detection is a separate step from repair. The goal is to find the exact spot before anyone breaks concrete or reroutes pipe. Hot water lines are frequent culprits, since heat cycles and hard water scale stress the pipe. Expansive and caliche soils in the region can also shift slabs over time. We confirm the leak is under the slab, then pinpoint it so you can choose the right repair.

localFactors.title: Warm Spots on Tile Floors
localFactors.body: Many Continental Ranch and Gladden Farms homes have tile over the slab. A hot water leak under tile can make one area feel warm to bare feet. Note where it is before we arrive.

localFactors.title: Soil Movement Under Slabs
localFactors.body: Expansive clay and caliche soils exist in the region, and they shift between wet monsoons and dry spells. That movement can stress pipes where they pass through or under concrete. New cracks in tile or drywall near a suspected leak are worth mentioning.

localFactors.title: Pools and Irrigation on the Meter
localFactors.body: Dove Mountain and other Marana homes with a pool autofill or heavy irrigation can mask a slab leak on the meter. We shut those off and isolate the house before testing. That keeps the result accurate.

localFactors.title: Older Versus Newer Slabs
localFactors.body: Continental Ranch slabs date to the 1990s and 2000s, while Saguaro Bloom and later Gladden Farms phases are newer. Older lines under a slab have had more years of hard water wear. Newer homes are less likely to leak but are not immune.

whatWeDo: We confirm a leak at the meter, then isolate hot from cold to see which side is losing water.
We pressure test the affected line to confirm the leak is under the slab and not in a wall or fixture.
We use acoustic listening and line tracing to pinpoint the spot on the floor.
We mark the location and show you what we found.
We explain repair options, from a spot repair to rerouting the line, and quote them upfront.

faqs.question: Why do slab leaks so often show up on hot water lines?
faqs.answer: Hot water lines expand and contract each time they heat and cool, which wears the pipe where it rubs against concrete or gravel. Hard water scale adds stress inside. Cold lines leak too, so we test both sides.

faqs.question: Will you have to break up my floor to find the leak?
faqs.answer: No. Detection happens from above the floor with pressure testing and listening equipment. Concrete is opened later, and only at the marked spot if you choose a spot repair.

faqs.question: Does homeowners insurance cover slab leak detection?
faqs.answer: Some policies cover the cost to find and access a slab leak, and some do not. Coverage varies, so call your insurer. We can provide documentation of what we found for your claim.

marana/slab-leak-repair.metaTitle: Slab Leak Repair in Marana, AZ | Wood's Plumbing
marana/slab-leak-repair.metaDescription: Slab leak repair in Marana: a spot repair through the floor or a reroute through walls and attic. Both priced upfront. ROC #296386. (520) 682-2233.
marana/slab-leak-repair.intro:
Once a slab leak is located, you have a decision to make. You can open the floor at the leak and repair that section. Or you can reroute the line above the slab and abandon the old pipe. Each option fits different homes, depending on the pipe's condition and where the leak sits.

In Marana, flooring and home age drive most of the decision. A single leak in a newer Gladden Farms or Saguaro Bloom home may suit a spot repair. A Continental Ranch home on its second slab leak in the same line often points toward a reroute. Large tile floors in Dove Mountain homes make breaking concrete disruptive and hard to patch. We lay out both paths with prices before you choose.

localFactors.title: Spot Repair Versus Reroute
localFactors.body: A spot repair fixes one leak and leaves the rest of the old pipe in the slab. A reroute runs a new line above the slab and bypasses the old one. If the pipe has leaked before, rerouting is usually the longer-term fix.

localFactors.title: Attic Heat and Insulation
localFactors.body: Rerouted lines in single-story Marana homes often run through the attic, which gets very hot in summer. We insulate those lines so cold water stays cool. That also helps protect them on winter freeze nights.

localFactors.title: Matching Tile After a Repair
localFactors.body: Many homes in Dove Mountain and Continental Ranch have tile across large areas. Matching discontinued tile after a spot repair can be hard. Factor that in when choosing between options.

localFactors.title: HOA Review for Exterior Runs
localFactors.body: Some reroutes run a line along an exterior wall or through the yard. In communities like Gladden Farms, exterior changes may need HOA approval. Check with your HOA if the plan includes outside work.

whatWeDo: We review the detection results and the pipe's history to decide which repairs make sense.
We quote a spot repair and a reroute side by side, so you can compare cost and disruption.
For a spot repair, we cut a small opening in the slab, replace the damaged section, and pressure test before closing it.
For a reroute, we run new line through walls and the attic, then disconnect and cap the old line under the slab.
We pressure test the finished work and tell you what flooring or drywall patching remains.

faqs.question: Is rerouting better than fixing the leak in the slab?
faqs.answer: It depends on the pipe. A first leak in fairly new pipe can often be handled with a spot repair. If your home has had more than one slab leak, rerouting avoids chasing the next one.

faqs.question: Will rerouting through the attic make my cold water warm in summer?
faqs.answer: Uninsulated lines in a Marana attic can deliver warm water from the cold tap in summer. We insulate rerouted lines to reduce this. Running the tap briefly clears water that sat in the line.

faqs.question: Who repairs the floor or drywall after a slab leak repair?
faqs.answer: We handle the plumbing and close the slab opening. Finished flooring, tile matching, and drywall texture usually go to a flooring or drywall contractor. We tell you what to expect before work starts so you can plan.

marana/tankless-water-heaters.metaTitle: Tankless Water Heaters in Marana, AZ | Wood's Plumbing
marana/tankless-water-heaters.metaDescription: Tankless water heater installs, descaling, and repair in Marana. We check gas line size and venting first, then quote upfront. ROC #296386. (520) 682-2233.
marana/tankless-water-heaters.intro:
Tankless water heaters heat water as it flows, so they do not run out during back-to-back showers. They also free up space in the garage. In Marana they suit many households, but hard water and gas supply both need attention before you switch.

Hard Tucson-area water leaves scale inside the heat exchanger. Without regular descaling, flow drops and error codes start. Gas tankless units also draw much more gas at once than a tank does. Older Continental Ranch and Cortaro gas lines may need upsizing to keep up. Some newer homes already have a larger line, which makes the switch easier. We install, descale, and repair tankless units. We also tell you honestly whether one fits your home, and what the switch would involve.

localFactors.title: Scale in the Heat Exchanger
localFactors.body: Hard water minerals build up inside a tankless unit's heat exchanger. Flushing it with a descaling solution on a regular schedule keeps flow and efficiency up. A softener or scale filter can stretch the time between flushes.

localFactors.title: Gas Line Sizing
localFactors.body: A gas tankless unit needs a large volume of gas when it fires. Older Continental Ranch and Cortaro homes often have lines sized for a tank heater. We measure the run and the total load before quoting.

localFactors.title: Venting and HOA Rules
localFactors.body: Tankless units vent through a wall or roof with dedicated pipe. In communities like Gladden Farms and Dove Mountain, exterior vent terminations may fall under HOA rules. Check before choosing a location.

localFactors.title: Freeze Risk Outdoors
localFactors.body: Outdoor tankless units rely on built-in heaters for freeze protection, which need power. Low areas near the Santa Cruz River and Avra Valley see colder nights. We cover placement and drain-down steps for power outages.

whatWeDo: We look at your hot water use, the current heater location, and the gas line and venting options.
We quote the unit and installation upfront, including any gas line or venting changes needed.
We mount the unit, connect gas and water, and install isolation valves so it can be descaled later.
We fire it, check gas pressure under full load, and test flow at your fixtures.
For existing tankless units, we descale the heat exchanger, clean the inlet filter, and review the error history.

faqs.question: How often should a tankless water heater be descaled in Marana?
faqs.answer: It depends on your water use and whether you have a softener. Hard water here builds scale faster than soft water does. Manufacturer manuals list a flushing interval, so we start there and adjust based on what we see inside.

faqs.question: Will a tankless unit work in an older Continental Ranch home?
faqs.answer: Often, yes, but the gas line is the usual hurdle. If the line cannot carry enough gas, it has to be upsized. We check this before quoting so the full cost is clear.

faqs.question: My tankless unit shows an error code and the water goes cold mid-shower. What causes that?
faqs.answer: Common causes are scale buildup, a clogged inlet filter, low gas supply, or a venting problem. Check whether your other gas appliances work normally. We read the error history and narrow it down on the visit.

marana/toilet-repair.metaTitle: Toilet Repair in Marana, AZ | Wood's Plumbing
marana/toilet-repair.metaDescription: Toilet repair in Marana: running toilets, weak flushes, leaks at the base and septic-safe fixes for 85653 and 85658 homes. Upfront pricing. (520) 682-2233.
marana/toilet-repair.intro:
Most toilet calls in Marana come down to three problems. The toilet keeps running, the flush is weak, or water appears around the base. Hard water plays a part in the first two. Minerals build up on fill valves, flappers and the small rim holes that direct water into the bowl.

Before you call, try a simple check. Put a few drops of food coloring in the tank and wait without flushing. Color in the bowl means the flapper is leaking. If the toilet rocks or water appears at the base, the wax seal on the slab flange has likely failed. We diagnose the cause on the visit and give you an upfront price. We also tell you plainly whether repair or replacement makes more sense.

localFactors.title: Scale on tank parts
localFactors.body: Marana's hard water leaves deposits on fill valves and flappers, which keeps them from sealing. Scale also narrows the rim jets, which shows up as a slow, weak flush.

localFactors.title: Original 1990s fixtures
localFactors.body: Many Continental Ranch homes still have their original toilets. Parts for some older models are harder to find, and the porcelain may be worth keeping or may be due for replacement.

localFactors.title: Running toilets on septic
localFactors.body: On septic properties near Picture Rocks and Avra Valley, a running toilet sends steady water into the tank and drain field. Fixing it quickly protects the septic system as well as the water bill.

localFactors.title: Slab flange seals
localFactors.body: Marana homes sit on concrete slabs, so the toilet bolts to a flange set in the floor. A rocking toilet breaks the wax seal, and water can travel under flooring before you see it.

whatWeDo: We watch a full flush cycle and check the tank parts, bowl and base for leaks or movement.
We test whether the flapper, fill valve or flush valve is causing a run or a weak flush.
We give you an upfront price for the repair and tell you if replacement is the better value.
We replace worn parts, clear scale from rim jets, or pull the toilet to reset the flange and wax seal.
We run several test flushes and check the base and supply connection for any drips.

faqs.question: Why does my toilet keep running in my Marana home?
faqs.answer: The usual cause is a flapper that no longer seals or a fill valve set too high. Hard water deposits make both worse over time. A dye test in the tank tells you which one is leaking.

faqs.question: Is it worth repairing the original toilet in my Continental Ranch house?
faqs.answer: It depends on the parts and the bowl. If tank parts are available and the porcelain is sound, repair is usually reasonable. If parts are hard to find or the flush stays weak, a new toilet may be the better choice.

faqs.question: Can a running toilet hurt my septic system near Avra Valley?
faqs.answer: Yes, it can. A constant flow adds water the septic system has to absorb, which can stress the drain field. Fix the leak promptly and avoid flushing wipes, even the ones labeled flushable.

marana/trenchless-sewer-repair.metaTitle: Trenchless Sewer Repair in Marana, AZ | Wood's Plumbing
marana/trenchless-sewer-repair.metaDescription: Trenchless sewer repair in Marana with pipe lining or bursting. Avoid digging through landscaping, pavers and caliche. Camera first. Call (520) 682-2233.
marana/trenchless-sewer-repair.intro:
Trenchless sewer repair fixes a damaged main line without digging a trench along its full length. There are two main methods. Pipe lining cures a new pipe inside the old one. Pipe bursting pulls a new pipe through while breaking the old one apart. Both need small access points instead of an open yard.

In Marana, trenchless repair often makes sense when a line runs under mature landscaping, pavers, a driveway or a Dove Mountain hardscape. It also saves time where caliche makes digging slow. It is not right for every line. A pipe with a deep sag usually needs excavation, because lining follows the existing shape. We start with a camera inspection, then give you an upfront price for the methods that will actually work.

localFactors.title: Hardscape and mature landscaping
localFactors.body: Dove Mountain and Marana Highlands yards often have pavers, desert landscaping and walls over the sewer line. Trenchless repair avoids tearing those out to reach the pipe.

localFactors.title: Caliche makes digging slow
localFactors.body: Caliche layers can make a traditional trench slow and labor heavy. Trenchless work limits digging to small access pits at each end of the repair.

localFactors.title: When sags rule out lining
localFactors.body: Settling soil can leave a belly in the line. Lining follows that low spot, so standing water remains. A deep sag usually needs a dig and replace for that section.

localFactors.title: Lines to septic tanks
localFactors.body: On properties near Avra Valley and Picture Rocks, the line from the house to the septic tank can often be lined or burst. The tank and drain field are separate from this repair.

whatWeDo: We camera the line to confirm the damage, measure its length and check for sags.
We explain whether lining, bursting or a traditional dig fits, and give you an upfront price.
We clean the line thoroughly, often with hydro jetting, to prepare it for repair.
We install the liner or pull the new pipe through, working from small access points.
We reopen any branch connections, run a final camera inspection and restore the access areas.

faqs.question: Can trenchless repair fix the sewer line under my Dove Mountain pavers?
faqs.answer: Often yes. If the camera shows cracks, roots or joint gaps without a major sag, lining or bursting can work. Your pavers and landscaping see little disturbance. HOAs may have rules on exterior work, so check with yours.

faqs.question: What is the difference between pipe lining and pipe bursting?
faqs.answer: Lining cures a new pipe inside the old one, keeping the same path. Bursting pulls a new pipe through while fracturing the old one outward. Bursting can replace badly collapsed pipe, while lining suits pipe that still holds its shape.

faqs.question: When is trenchless repair not a good fit in Marana?
faqs.answer: A deep belly, a fully collapsed section that a burst head cannot pass, or a line needing a slope correction usually needs excavation. We show you the camera footage and explain why before recommending a method.

marana/water-heater-installation.metaTitle: Water Heater Installation in Marana, AZ | Wood's Plumbing

localFactors.title: Casitas and Guest Suites
localFactors.body: Dove Mountain and other larger Marana lots often include a casita. A separate heater there avoids waiting for hot water to travel from the main house. We size it to the fixtures it will serve.

localFactors.title: Gas Line Capacity
localFactors.body: Adding a gas water heater means checking whether the existing gas line can supply it along with the furnace, range, and other appliances. An undersized line causes poor burner performance. We confirm capacity before quoting.

localFactors.title: HOA Rules on Outdoor Units
localFactors.body: Communities like Gladden Farms, Saguaro Bloom, and Dove Mountain may have HOA rules about exterior equipment and vent locations. Check with your HOA before choosing an exterior wall. We can give you the unit details for your request.

localFactors.title: Drain Paths on a Slab
localFactors.body: A new location needs a route for the relief valve line and a drain pan where required. On a slab home with no nearby drain, that route takes planning. We map it before any work starts.

whatWeDo: We visit the site and look at where the heater will go, the fixtures it will serve, and the gas or electrical supply available.

We give you an upfront price for the plumbing, gas, and venting work, and note if an electrician is needed for a new circuit.

faqs.question: Can you add a water heater to a casita on my Dove Mountain property?
faqs.answer: Usually, yes. We look at whether the casita has its own gas or enough electrical capacity, and where the unit can vent and drain. Then we quote the job with those details spelled out.

faqs.question: Do I need a permit to install a water heater in a new location in Marana?
faqs.answer: New installations and relocations often require a permit through the Town of Marana, or Pima County for properties outside town limits. We handle the permit as part of the job when one is required.

faqs.question: Can I move my water heater out of the garage?
faqs.answer: It is possible, but it adds work. The new spot needs water lines, gas or power, venting, and a safe discharge for the relief valve. We walk through the cost and tradeoffs so you can decide if the move is worth it.

marana/water-heater-repair.metaTitle: Water Heater Repair in Marana, AZ | Wood's Plumbing
marana/water-heater-repair.metaDescription: Water heater repair in Marana for gas and electric tanks in garages from Dove Mountain to Cortaro. We test parts and quote first. Call (520) 682-2233.
marana/water-heater-repair.intro:
Most Marana water heaters sit in the garage, where summer heat and winter cold both reach them. Repair makes sense when the tank itself is sound and a part has failed. On a gas unit that might be the thermocouple, igniter, or gas control. On an electric unit it is usually an element or thermostat.

Hard water is the other big factor here. Sediment settles at the bottom of the tank, causes popping and rumbling, and wears out parts faster. We test the components, check the tank for leaks, and tell you plainly whether a repair is worth the money. If the tank body is leaking, no part will fix it, and we will say so before you spend anything.

localFactors.title: Sediment From Hard Water
localFactors.body: Minerals in Tucson-area water settle on the tank floor. On gas units this causes rumbling and overheating at the bottom. On electric units it can bury and burn out the lower element.

localFactors.title: Garage Dust and Pilot Outages
localFactors.body: Gas water heaters in hot, dusty Marana garages can pull lint and dust into the burner area. That buildup can choke the air supply and cause pilot or burner outages. Keeping boxes and clutter away from the base helps.

localFactors.title: Pressure Regulators and Drips
localFactors.body: Homes with a pressure regulator on the main line create a closed system. Heated water has nowhere to expand without a working expansion tank. A failed one can make the relief valve drip onto the garage floor.

localFactors.title: Electric Units on Rural Lots
localFactors.body: Properties toward Avra Valley and Picture Rocks without gas service often run electric water heaters. Elements and thermostats are the common repairs there. A tripped high-limit reset is another frequent cause of no hot water.

whatWeDo: We confirm whether the unit is gas or electric and ask what changed: no hot water, short hot water, noise, or a leak.
We test the pilot assembly, burner, and gas control, or the elements and thermostats with a meter, depending on the type.
We inspect the relief valve, drain valve, and connections, and look at the tank body for rust or seepage.
We tell you what failed, quote the repair, and say honestly if the tank is near the end of its life.
After the repair we confirm the unit heats properly and that every connection stays dry.

faqs.question: My water heater pops and rumbles. Is it about to fail?
faqs.answer: Not always. The noise usually comes from hard water sediment at the bottom of the tank. Flushing can help if the buildup is light, but heavy buildup on an older tank is a sign to start planning ahead.

faqs.question: Why does the relief valve on my garage water heater keep dripping?
faqs.answer: It may be releasing pressure from heat expansion, especially in homes with a pressure regulator and no working expansion tank. It can also be a worn valve. Never cap or plug it, because that valve prevents a dangerous pressure buildup.

faqs.question: Is it worth repairing an older water heater?
faqs.answer: It depends on the part and the tank. A new igniter or element on a dry, sound tank can be a reasonable repair. If the tank shows rust at the base or seepage, we would steer you toward replacement instead.

marana/water-heater-replacement.metaTitle: Water Heater Replacement in Marana, AZ | Wood's Plumbing

localFactors.title: Signs the Tank Is Done
localFactors.body: Water around the base, rust streaks on the tank, or a metallic smell in the hot water point to a failing tank. Hard water sediment speeds up the corrosion. Replacing parts will not fix a leaking tank body.

localFactors.title: Garage Swaps in Continental Ranch
localFactors.body: Most homes in Continental Ranch and Cortaro keep the heater in the garage. That makes a like-for-like replacement straightforward. We check the stand, drain pan, and venting while we are there.

localFactors.title: Upsizing for Growing Households
localFactors.body: Families in Gladden Farms and Saguaro Bloom sometimes outgrow the original tank size. If you run out of hot water often, a larger tank or a tankless unit may fit better. We size it to how your household uses water.

localFactors.title: Replace Before It Floods
localFactors.body: A garage tank that fails can soak storage boxes and drywall. If yours is older and showing rust, replacing it on your schedule beats an emergency swap. We can quote it ahead of time.

whatWeDo: We confirm the tank is failing and not just a part, so you do not replace a heater that could be repaired.

faqs.question: My Continental Ranch water heater is leaking from the bottom. Can it be fixed?
faqs.answer: If the water is coming from the tank body, no. That means the inner tank has corroded through, and the heater needs to be replaced. If the leak is from a fitting or the drain valve, a repair may still work, so we check first.

faqs.question: Should I replace my tank with the same size?
faqs.answer: Not always. If your household has grown or you often run short on hot water, a larger tank or a tankless unit may suit you better. If the current size works, matching it keeps the job simpler.

faqs.question: Will a new water heater need anything extra in my home?

marana/water-softener-installation.metaTitle: Water Softener Installation in Marana, AZ | Wood's Plumbing
marana/water-softener-installation.metaDescription: Water softener installation in Marana for hard water scale. Garage loops, new loops, well and septic homes. Upfront pricing. Call (520) 682-2233. ROC #296386.
marana/water-softener-installation.intro:
Marana's water is hard, and you can see it in white crust on faucets, spotted shower glass and scale in the water heater. A water softener treats every gallon entering the house, so fixtures, the water heater and appliances all see less mineral buildup. It does not filter drinking water; that is a separate job for a reverse osmosis system.

Most installs here go in the garage, close to where the main line enters. Many newer homes in Gladden Farms and Saguaro Bloom already have a softener loop stubbed out near the water heater. Older Continental Ranch homes and rural properties often need a loop added. We look at your plumbing, drain options and water source, then give you an upfront price before we start.

localFactors.title: Pre-plumbed garage loops
localFactors.body: Many 2000s and newer Marana homes have a capped softener loop in the garage. When it is there and in good shape, installation is mostly connecting the unit, the drain line and an electrical outlet.

localFactors.title: Continental Ranch retrofits
localFactors.body: Some 1990s homes in Continental Ranch were built without a loop. We cut into the main line where it enters the garage. We add a bypass so the softener can be serviced without shutting off the house.

localFactors.title: Wells near Avra Valley
localFactors.body: Well water can carry iron, sediment or other minerals that foul a softener resin bed. We recommend a water test first, and some wells need a sediment filter installed ahead of the softener.

localFactors.title: Septic and brine discharge
localFactors.body: A softener flushes salty brine during regeneration. On homes with septic toward Picture Rocks and Avra Valley, we talk through where that discharge goes before choosing the drain point.

whatWeDo: We find your main line entry, check for an existing loop and confirm a drain and outlet are nearby.
We ask about your water source, household size and any well or septic system to size the unit.
We give you an upfront price for the softener, any loop work and the drain connection.
We install the softener with a bypass valve, connect the drain with an air gap and load the salt.
We set the regeneration schedule, test the softened water at a faucet and show you how to use the bypass.

faqs.question: How do I know if my Marana home already has a softener loop?
faqs.answer: Look in the garage near the water heater for two capped pipes coming out of the wall, often with a nearby drain and outlet. If you are unsure, send us a photo or we can check on a visit.

faqs.question: Should my Gladden Farms home get a softener or reverse osmosis?
faqs.answer: They do different jobs. A softener reduces scale throughout the whole house. Reverse osmosis filters drinking water at one faucet. Many households with hard water use both, with the softener protecting the RO membrane.

faqs.question: Can I put a softener on a well in the Avra Valley area?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but test the water first. Iron and sediment can shorten resin life, so some wells need filtration ahead of the softener. We size the system around what the test shows.

marana/whole-house-repiping.metaTitle: Whole House Repiping in Marana, AZ | Wood's Plumbing
marana/whole-house-repiping.metaDescription: Whole house repiping in Marana for repeat slab leaks, pinhole copper leaks and older supply lines. Attic reroutes with PEX. Call (520) 682-2233. ROC #296386.
marana/whole-house-repiping.intro:
Repiping replaces every water supply line in the house at once. In Marana, it usually comes up after a second or third slab leak, or when pinhole leaks keep appearing in copper lines. At that point, patching one spot at a time costs more and disrupts more than a full replacement.

Most Marana homes were built with supply lines running through or under the concrete slab. A repipe typically abandons those lines and reroutes new PEX through the attic, dropping down through walls to each fixture. That avoids breaking up floors. The work involves small drywall openings, which are patched afterward. We inspect the home first, explain whether a repipe is warranted, and give you an upfront price for the full project.

localFactors.title: Repeat slab leaks
localFactors.body: Homes in Continental Ranch and other 1990s subdivisions often have copper running under the slab. Once one leak appears, others can follow, and a reroute overhead takes the slab out of the picture.

localFactors.title: Hard water and copper pinholes
localFactors.body: Mineral-heavy water combined with older copper can lead to small pinhole leaks. When they show up in multiple places, the problem is the piping, not a single bad spot.

localFactors.title: Summer attic heat
localFactors.body: Marana attics get very hot from June through September. We schedule attic work for cooler parts of the day and support and insulate PEX properly so it stays protected from heat.

localFactors.title: Larger homes and rural properties
localFactors.body: Larger Dove Mountain homes have long runs to distant bathrooms, so a manifold layout can balance flow. Older rural homes near Avra Valley may have mixed or galvanized piping that we assess separately.

whatWeDo: We inspect the current piping, review your leak history and check water pressure.
We explain whether repiping is warranted and lay out the attic route and fixture drops.
We give you an upfront price covering materials, labor, permit and drywall openings.
We install the new PEX system, connect each fixture and the water heater, and abandon the old lines.
We pressure test the system, complete the inspection and patch the access openings.

faqs.question: When does repiping make more sense than fixing another slab leak?
faqs.answer: If your Marana home has had more than one slab leak, or pinhole leaks keep appearing, a repipe is worth pricing. It addresses the whole system instead of the next weak spot. We compare both options on the visit.

faqs.question: Will repiping my Continental Ranch home mean tearing up floors?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The new lines run through the attic and down inside walls, so the slab stays intact. You will see small drywall openings at fixtures, which get patched when the work is done.

faqs.question: Is PEX in a hot Marana attic a problem?
faqs.answer: Not when it is installed correctly. PEX handles heat well when it is supported, kept out of sunlight and covered by attic insulation. We plan the route so lines stay buried in insulation where possible.

northwest-tucson/drain-cleaning.intro:
Slow drains in Northwest Tucson usually have an older cause than a hair clog. Homes in Linda Vista, La Cholla and Overton often have clay sewer laterals or cast iron drains under the slab. Mature mesquite and palo verde trees planted decades ago now send roots toward every joint that leaks moisture.

Wood's Plumbing has cleared drains across the Tucson area since 1979, and our shop sits just north in Marana. We start by finding where the blockage is and what it is made of. A kitchen grease clog, a root mass at a clay joint and scale inside cast iron each need a different tool. We tell you which one we found, give an upfront price, and show you camera footage when it helps you decide what comes next.

localFactors.title: Tree roots in clay joints
localFactors.body: Clay laterals from the 1970s were laid in short sections with joints every few feet. Mesquite and palo verde roots find those joints and can fill the pipe over a few seasons.

localFactors.title: Scale inside cast iron
localFactors.body: Cast iron drains rust and build rough scale on the inside as they age. Paper and grease catch on that rough surface, so clogs return faster than in newer plastic lines.

localFactors.title: Long kitchen drain runs
localFactors.body: Many older ranch homes have the kitchen at the far end from the sewer exit. Grease cools and settles along that long horizontal run under the slab.

localFactors.title: Debris after monsoon storms
localFactors.body: Yard drains, patio drains and cleanouts with loose caps can take in silt and gravel during heavy summer rain. That material settles in the lateral and slows the whole house.

whatWeDo: We ask which fixtures are slow and run water to see whether the problem is one drain or the main line.
We open the nearest cleanout, or the roof vent when no cleanout exists, to reach the blockage.
We clear it with a cable machine sized for the pipe, using a root cutting head when roots are present.
On main line clogs we can run a camera to look for cracked clay, offset joints or failing cast iron.
We explain what we found and whether the line needs repair or just routine cleaning.

faqs.question: Why does my main drain in Orange Grove keep clogging every year?
faqs.answer: Repeat clogs on a schedule often point to roots growing back into a clay joint. Cleaning cuts the roots but does not seal the joint. A camera inspection shows whether a spot repair or liner would stop the cycle.

faqs.question: Can I use chemical drain cleaner on old cast iron pipes?
faqs.answer: We advise against it. Harsh chemicals can sit on the bottom of rusted cast iron and speed up the wear. They also make the drain unsafe for whoever clears it later.

faqs.question: My house does not have an outdoor cleanout. Can you still clean the main line?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many older Northwest Tucson homes lack an accessible cleanout, so we may go through a roof vent or pull a toilet. We can also install a cleanout so future service is easier and less costly.

localFactors.title: Original valves that will not turn
localFactors.body: Many 1970s and 1980s homes still have gate valves at the main and under sinks. After years of mineral buildup they often seize or snap when someone forces them during a leak.

localFactors.title: Pinholes in aging copper
localFactors.body: Hard water slowly thins copper from the inside. In older Northwest Tucson homes, that wear can show up as a sudden spray behind a wall or a hot spot in the slab.

localFactors.title: Monsoon sewer backups
localFactors.body: Heavy July to September storms can push water into cracked clay laterals. Older neighborhoods near the Rillito and Cañada del Oro washes may see drains back up during or after a storm.

localFactors.title: Freeze damage on exposed lines
localFactors.body: Older homes often have hose bibs and pipes on exterior walls with little insulation. A rare hard freeze can split them, and the leak appears when the day warms up.

whatWeDo: We talk you through closing the main shutoff, or the meter valve if the house valve is stuck.

faqs.question: My main shutoff in my Casas Adobes house will not budge. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Do not force it with a wrench, because old gate valves can break and make the leak worse. Use the curb valve at the water meter if you can reach it safely. Then call us, and we can replace the seized valve during the same visit.

faqs.question: Is a sewer backup during a monsoon storm an emergency?
faqs.answer: Yes, if sewage is coming up into tubs, showers or floor drains. Stop using water in the house so you do not add to the backup. Older clay laterals in Northwest Tucson often have cracks or roots that storms expose, and we can clear and inspect the line.

faqs.question: Do you charge more for a call at night or on a weekend?

northwest-tucson/sewer-line-repair.intro:

localFactors.title: Clay laterals with root damage
localFactors.body: Clay pipe was common when many Northwest Tucson homes were built. Mesquite and palo verde roots can crack or crush it, not just clog it.

localFactors.title: Cast iron under the slab
localFactors.body: Cast iron drains beneath older homes can corrode along the bottom of the pipe. Water then leaks into the soil under the floor, which can be hard to notice.

localFactors.title: Sags from soil settling
localFactors.body: Expansive soils and settling fill can create low spots, called bellies, in the line. Waste collects there and causes repeat backups.

localFactors.title: Trees near the sewer path
localFactors.body: Mature trees planted in front yards decades ago often sit right over the lateral. Repair plans need to account for roots and for protecting the tree where possible.

whatWeDo: We clear any blockage so the camera can travel the full length of the line.
We record a camera inspection and locate problem spots and their depth from above ground.
We show you the footage and explain spot repair, section replacement or full replacement options.

faqs.question: How do I know if my sewer line is broken or just clogged?
faqs.answer: Clogs that return after cleaning, sewage odors in the yard, or gurgling drains all point to damage. Soggy or extra green patches over the sewer path are another sign. A camera inspection is the clearest way to know.

faqs.question: Can you fix a clay sewer line without replacing the whole thing?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the damage is limited to one or two spots and the rest of the line is sound. We replace the bad section with modern pipe and proper couplings. If the camera shows damage along most of the line, partial repairs may not hold up.

faqs.question: What about the cast iron drain under my house?
faqs.answer: Cast iron under the slab is harder to reach than a yard lateral. Options include opening the floor for a section repair or rerouting the drain. We camera the line first and explain the tradeoffs before you commit.

northwest-tucson/slab-leak-detection.intro:
Many Northwest Tucson homes built from the 1970s to the 1990s have copper water lines buried in or under the concrete slab. Over decades, hard water wears copper from the inside. Pipes can also rub against gravel or concrete as expansive soil shifts, until a pinhole opens where no one can see it.

Wood's Plumbing has found and fixed leaks in the Tucson area since 1979. Slab leak detection is about locating the leak before anyone breaks concrete. We isolate hot and cold lines, test for pressure loss, and use listening and thermal tools to narrow the spot. You get a clear location, what we think caused it, and repair options with upfront prices. Finding the right spot first keeps the repair smaller and saves your flooring.

localFactors.title: Copper under older slabs
localFactors.body: Homes in Casas Adobes, Linda Vista and the Ina Road corridor commonly have copper buried below the floor. Age and hard water make pinhole leaks more likely in these lines.

localFactors.title: Expansive soil movement
localFactors.body: Clay heavy soils in parts of the region swell when wet and shrink when dry. That movement can stress pipes at points where they pass through the slab.

localFactors.title: Hot leaks cause warm floors
localFactors.body: A leak on the hot side often makes a warm spot on tile or concrete. Many people notice it first with bare feet or when a pet keeps lying in one spot.

localFactors.title: Leaks that hide under tile
localFactors.body: Older homes often have tile laid directly over the slab. Water can travel along the pipe before it surfaces, so the damp spot may not be above the leak.

whatWeDo: We check your water meter with all fixtures off to confirm water is being lost.
We isolate hot and cold lines to learn which side is leaking.
We use acoustic listening and thermal imaging to trace the line and find the loudest point.
We mark the leak location on the floor and explain what we found.
We give you upfront prices for spot repair, rerouting or repiping so you can choose.

faqs.question: How can I check for a slab leak myself before calling?
faqs.answer: Turn off every faucet, appliance and irrigation line, then watch the small leak indicator on your water meter. If it keeps moving, water is going somewhere. Also look for warm floor spots, a running water sound when nothing is on, or a jump in your water bill.

faqs.question: Do you have to break up my floor to find the leak?
faqs.answer: No. Detection is done with pressure tests, listening equipment and thermal imaging from above the floor. Concrete stays in place unless you choose a spot repair after we find the leak.

faqs.question: My house had one slab leak years ago. Should I expect more?
faqs.answer: A second leak is fairly common in older copper systems, since the same water and age affect all of the pipe. One repair does not mean the rest is worn out. We can look at the overall line condition and help you decide on spot repair versus a reroute.

northwest-tucson/slab-leak-repair.metaDescription: Slab leak repair in Northwest Tucson: spot repair, reroute through walls or attic, or repipe for older copper. Upfront pricing. ROC #296386. (520) 682-2233.

Then we do the work cleanly, test it, and tell you what to expect from the rest of the system.

localFactors.title: Tile floors in older homes
localFactors.body: Many 1970s and 1980s houses in Casas Adobes and Orange Grove have tile set on the slab. Matching discontinued tile after a spot repair can be hard, which often favors a reroute.

localFactors.title: Attic heat for reroutes
localFactors.body: Rerouted lines often run through the attic, which gets very hot in summer. We insulate attic lines and schedule attic work for cooler parts of the day.

localFactors.title: Repeat leaks in aging copper
localFactors.body: If a home has had two or more slab leaks, the copper is likely thinning throughout. Spot repairs can turn into a series of break ins.

localFactors.title: Soil and slab conditions
localFactors.body: Caliche and compacted fill under older slabs can make digging slow. We plan the access hole to keep the opening as small as practical.

faqs.question: Is it better to reroute or jackhammer the slab in an older Northwest Tucson home?
faqs.answer: A reroute avoids breaking floors and bypasses the whole leaking run. A spot repair can make sense for a first leak in an easy location. We weigh flooring, access and pipe age with you before you decide.

faqs.question: Will rerouting a line through my attic cause problems in summer?
faqs.answer: Lines in the attic are insulated to protect them from heat and the occasional freeze. You may notice warmer cold water for a few seconds at first. Most homeowners find this a reasonable tradeoff for avoiding floor demolition.

faqs.question: After a repair, how do I know the rest of my copper is okay?
faqs.answer: We pressure test the whole system once the repair is done. That confirms no other active leaks at the time. It cannot predict future wear, so watch your meter and water bill as part of normal upkeep.

northwest-tucson/tankless-water-heaters.metaTitle: Tankless Water Heaters NW Tucson | Wood's Plumbing
northwest-tucson/tankless-water-heaters.metaDescription: Tankless water heater installs in Northwest Tucson, with gas line sizing and venting checks for 1970s to 2000s homes. Call Wood's Plumbing: (520) 682-2233.

localFactors.title: Undersized gas piping
localFactors.body: Older homes often have smaller gas lines that cannot feed a large tankless burner. Some installs need a new line from the meter, which we include in the quote.

localFactors.title: Venting on older walls
localFactors.body: Tankless units need specific vent materials and clearances. On older block or frame walls we plan a route that clears windows, eaves and property lines.

localFactors.title: Scale in the heat exchanger
localFactors.body: Hard Tucson water builds scale inside tankless heat exchangers. Regular descaling, or a softener ahead of the unit, keeps it running as designed.

localFactors.title: Panel capacity for electric units
localFactors.body: Whole house electric tankless models draw a lot of current. Many older Northwest Tucson panels lack the spare capacity without an electrical upgrade.

whatWeDo: We review your hot water use and where the current heater sits.
We measure gas line sizes and lengths, or check panel capacity for an electric unit.
We pick a mounting and vent location and explain any gas or electrical work required.

faqs.question: Can my 1980s Northwest Tucson house support a gas tankless heater?
faqs.answer: Often it can, but the gas line may need to be upsized. We check the meter, pipe diameter and total run before recommending a unit. If an upgrade is needed, it is part of the upfront quote.

faqs.question: How often does a tankless unit need descaling with our water?
faqs.answer: It depends on your water use and whether you have a softener. Hard water in this area makes regular descaling important. We install service valves so the job is quick and can show you what to watch for.

faqs.question: Is tankless always the right choice over a new tank?
faqs.answer: No. Tankless saves space and gives continuous hot water, but upfront cost is higher in older homes that need gas or electrical work. For some households a standard or high efficiency tank is the better value, and we will say so.

northwest-tucson/water-heater-repair.metaDescription: Water heater repair in Northwest Tucson for older garage tanks: sediment, pilot and thermocouple faults, leaking valves. Upfront pricing. Call (520) 682-2233.

localFactors.title: Sediment from hard water
localFactors.body: Tucson water carries a lot of minerals. They settle in the tank and harden into a layer that makes popping noises and wastes energy on gas units.

localFactors.title: Garage heat and pilot issues
localFactors.body: Older standing pilot gas heaters in hot garages can have pilot outages and thermocouple wear. Dust from the garage also clogs combustion air openings.

localFactors.title: Closet installs in older homes

We look at the age, anode condition, venting and relief valve to judge if repair is sensible.
We give you an upfront repair price, and a replacement price if the tank itself is failing.
After repair we confirm safe operation, proper venting and correct water temperature.

faqs.question: My water heater in the garage makes popping sounds. Is it about to fail?
faqs.answer: Popping usually means hard water sediment is trapped under the water at the tank bottom. A flush can help if the buildup is not severe. If the tank is old and the layer has hardened, flushing may not fix it and replacement becomes the better choice.

faqs.question: Water is dripping from the pipe on the side of my tank. What is that?
faqs.answer: That pipe drains the temperature and pressure relief valve. A drip can mean a worn valve, high water pressure, or a missing expansion tank. We test the pressure and the valve so the cause gets fixed, not just the part.

faqs.question: How do I know if repair makes sense on an older Northwest Tucson heater?
faqs.answer: Check the label for the manufacture date and look for rust or water at the base. Valve and part repairs are often reasonable on a sound tank. A leaking tank cannot be repaired, and we will tell you plainly when that is the case.

A house in Overton or Cortaro Farms built in the 1980s may have venting, gas piping and water connections that no longer match current code. Today's tanks can also be taller or wider than the one being removed, which matters in a closet install.

Wood's Plumbing has installed water heaters across the Tucson area since 1979, under Arizona ROC #296386. Before we quote, we look at the space, the vent, the gas line and the shutoff. We then explain your choices, such as tank size, gas or electric, and standard or high efficiency. You get an upfront price that includes the updates your home actually needs, so the bill on install day matches the quote.

localFactors.title: Older venting and clearances
localFactors.body: Vent pipes in 1970s and 1980s garages may be the wrong size or in poor shape for a new gas heater. We check draft and clearance before choosing a model.

localFactors.title: Tight closet dimensions
localFactors.body: Interior closets in older Linda Vista and Casas Adobes homes were sized for older tanks. We measure height, width and door clearance so the new unit fits and can be serviced.

localFactors.title: Pressure and expansion tanks
localFactors.body: Many older homes never had a thermal expansion tank. Current installs often need one, especially where a pressure reducing valve is present.

localFactors.title: Hard water and tank life
localFactors.body: Mineral heavy water shortens tank life in this region. We can talk about anode choices and flushing, or a softener, so the new heater lasts longer.

whatWeDo: We look at your current heater, the space, the vent, the gas or electrical supply and the water connections.
We help you choose capacity and fuel type based on your household and how you use hot water.

faqs.question: Will a new water heater fit in the same closet as my old one?
faqs.answer: Not always. Newer tanks can be larger than older ones with the same capacity. We measure the space before quoting, and if it is tight we will suggest a model or size that fits and meets clearance needs.

faqs.question: Should I switch from a gas tank to electric in my older home?
faqs.answer: It depends on your electrical panel, the cost of each fuel for your household, and how much hot water you use. Some older Northwest Tucson homes would need panel or wiring upgrades for a large electric unit. We can lay out the tradeoffs so you can decide.

faqs.question: Why does my replacement quote include parts my old heater never had?
faqs.answer: Code and manufacturer requirements have changed since many older homes were built. Items such as an expansion tank, a drain pan or updated venting may now be required. We list each item so you can see why it is there.

northwest-tucson/water-softener-installa.metaDescription: Water softener installation in Northwest Tucson, including new loops for older homes without one. Protect water heaters and fixtures. Call (520) 682-2233.
northwest-tucson/water-softener-installa.intro:
Tucson-area water is hard, and Northwest Tucson homeowners see it as white crust on faucets, spotted dishes and scale in the water heater. Newer homes are often built with a softener loop already in the garage. Many 1970s and 1980s houses in Casas Adobes, Thornydale and Linda Vista were not. Installing a softener there means adding that plumbing first.

Wood's Plumbing has served the Tucson area since 1979, and we install water softeners. We find your main line, decide where the unit and its drain should go, and plan a bypass for outdoor hose bibs and irrigation. Then we give you an upfront price for the softener and the plumbing work. Softer water is easier on your water heater, fixtures and appliances in a region with this much mineral content.

localFactors.title: No softener loop in older homes
localFactors.body: Many older Northwest Tucson houses have the main line entering at a wall or under the slab with no loop. We cut in a new loop where the line is reachable, often in the garage.

localFactors.title: Finding a drain for regeneration
localFactors.body: A softener needs a drain for its regeneration cycle. In older garages without a laundry nearby, we plan a code compliant drain route.

localFactors.title: Keeping irrigation on hard water
localFactors.body: Older homes often have hose bibs and drip lines teed off the same main. We set up the loop so outdoor water bypasses the softener and does not waste salt.

localFactors.title: Scale on aging water heaters
localFactors.body: Hard water builds scale in tanks and tankless units. Adding a softener can help a newer heater hold up better in this climate.

whatWeDo: We locate your main water line and see where a loop, power outlet and drain can go.
We discuss softener size based on your household and water use.
You get an upfront price for the unit plus the loop, bypass valve and drain work.
We install the loop and bypass, set the softener, and connect the drain line.
We program the unit, check for leaks, and show you how to add salt and use the bypass.

faqs.question: My older home does not have a softener loop. Can I still get a softener?
faqs.answer: Yes. We add a loop by cutting into the main supply where it is accessible, usually near where it enters the house. We also add a bypass valve so you can isolate the softener for service.

faqs.question: Should my outdoor faucets and drip system run through the softener?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Softened water is not needed for plants and uses salt you do not need to spend. If your irrigation tees off the main inside the loop, we can re-pipe it to stay on hard water.

faqs.question: Will a water softener fix pinhole leaks in my copper pipes?
faqs.answer: No, and we will not claim it will. A softener reduces scale on fixtures and in water heaters. Copper leaks have several causes, and existing pipe wear will not reverse.

northwest-tucson/whole-house-repiping.metaTitle: Whole House Repiping in NW Tucson | Wood's Plumbing
northwest-tucson/whole-house-repiping.metaDescription: Whole house repiping for Northwest Tucson homes with galvanized or worn copper lines. PEX or copper options, upfront pricing, ROC #296386. Call (520) 682-2233.
northwest-tucson/whole-house-repiping.intro:
Repiping makes the most sense in Northwest Tucson homes where the original supply lines are reaching the end of their life. Some older houses in Casas Adobes and Orange Grove still have galvanized steel, which rusts inside and chokes water flow. Others have copper that has already sprung more than one pinhole leak under the slab.

Wood's Plumbing has repiped homes in the Tucson area since 1979, under Arizona ROC #296386. A repipe replaces the supply lines with new pipe routed through the attic and walls instead of under the floor. We plan the routes, explain material choices such as PEX or copper, and give you an upfront price for the full scope. That includes the openings we make and how they get patched.

localFactors.title: Galvanized lines in older homes
localFactors.body: Galvanized steel rusts from the inside out. Signs include low pressure at several fixtures and brown or rusty water after the lines sit unused.

localFactors.title: Copper with a leak history
localFactors.body: Hard water wears copper over decades. Homes that have had two or more slab leaks often save money over time with a repipe instead of more spot repairs.

localFactors.title: Attic routing and summer heat
localFactors.body: New lines usually run through the attic in single story Northwest Tucson homes. They are insulated, and we plan attic work around the hottest part of the day.

localFactors.title: Mixed materials from past repairs
localFactors.body: Older houses often have patches of copper, galvanized and plastic from earlier fixes. Mixed metals can corrode at the joints, and a repipe replaces them all.

whatWeDo: We inspect the existing pipe, test water pressure, and map where lines run now.
We plan new routes through the attic and walls and explain PEX and copper options.
You get an upfront price that includes the pipe, fittings, valves, wall openings and patching.
We install the new system, usually room by room, and connect each fixture and the water heater.
We pressure test, flush the lines, patch the openings, and walk you through the new shutoffs.

faqs.question: How do I know if my Northwest Tucson home has galvanized pipe?
faqs.answer: Look at the pipe near your water heater or main shutoff. Galvanized is dull gray steel with threaded fittings, and a magnet sticks to it. Copper is reddish brown and a magnet will not stick.

faqs.question: Should I choose PEX or copper for my repipe?
faqs.answer: PEX is flexible, needs fewer fittings and handles occasional freezes well. Copper is rigid, long proven, and preferred by some homeowners. We explain the cost and installation differences for your house so you can choose.

faqs.question: Can my family live in the house during a repipe?
faqs.answer: Usually yes. Water is shut off during parts of the work day and restored most evenings. We will tell you the expected schedule and which rooms we need to access each day.
